title: Queue-flush tiny-debug notes (lunch experiments)
content:
12:10pm — lunchtime micro-session. Goal: quick repro + cheap hypothesis checks for intermittent tiny-tail latency spikes when prefix cache is warm but queue depth == 1.

What I observed (recap):
- Production symptoms: ~0.5% of requests in a 5m window show 95th > 120ms for short prompts (~32 tokens), overall p99 still fine.
- Pattern: Happens when autoscaler recently shrank instance count or when model switched quantization profile (int8->int4 fallback) for a few minutes.
- Logs: there are repeated "kv-cache miss then load" events but timestamps show load latency fluctuates (20–60ms).

Quick local repro notes (commands I used):
- ./scripts/run_local_worker.sh --model gpt-small --seq 32 --profile int4 --port 5050
- ./tools/requester --concurrency 1 --qps 30 --payload samples/prompt-short.txt --target http://localhost:5050/gen
- To trace KV latency: tcpdump -i lo -w kv-traffic.pcap port 6000 &
- Collected runtime debug: /debug/kv/stats -> shows "flush_count" increments coincident with the spikes

Small snippets from debug logs (sanitized):
- [14:03:11.321] kv-cache: lookup key=abcd... hit=false
- [14:03:11.347] kv-cache: async-load start id=42 src=fs shard=3
- [14:03:11.409] kv-cache: async-load complete id=42 took=62ms size=1.2KB
- [14:03:11.420] runtime: apply-kv took=4ms total-req=66ms

Hypotheses (quick):
1) Eviction/compaction running concurrently when queue depth low -> causes background I/O burst and blocks async-loads briefly.
2) Kernel scheduling/affinity shift (when autoscaler terminates a pod) leads to short-lived CPU starvation for the worker thread handling async loads.
3) Small pathological path in int4 fallback code that forces a sync path occasionally for the first token after a quant profile swap.

Experiments run & results: (all < 30 min)
- Disabled eviction in local config -> 0.15% spikes remain but reduced amplitude (max 45ms). Suggests eviction is partial contributor.
- Pin worker thread to CPU core with taskset -> spikes drop to ~0.08% and peaks mid-40ms. CPU pin helps.
- Forced quant profile swap repeatedly -> reproducible 1-in-200 spike where kv-load shows 80–120ms. So quant swap seems to be a clear trigger for some cases.

Immediate TODOs (priority):
- [ ] Add metric: "kv_async_load_latency_bucket" with labels {shard, cause} — helps separate eviction vs cold-loads (P0)
- [ ] Add small guard: when quant profile changes, pre-warm KV for top-10 prefixes before routing production traffic (P1)
- [ ] Add runtime option: delay autoscaler termination by 10s to observe effect of graceful drain on spikes (P2)
- [ ] Create minimal unit test that simulates quant-profile swap and asserts no sync-load path (P1)

Notes for PR (what to change):
- In kv cache loader: move heavy compaction to background tokio task with lower priority and yield points. Also add prometheus timing for compaction wall-time.
- In runtime: add hooks on model-profile-change to trigger prewarm async loads for a small set of frequently used tokens. This should be configurable per-deployment.

Questions to ping folks:
- @Aisha: can you share recent eviction compaction flags? I think default compact_threshold is too aggressive after a cold restart.
- @Diego: can you reproduce the quant-profile swap behavior on your AMD nodes? suspect hardware differences.

Quick sketches of acceptance criteria:
- Spikes (95th of the short prompt workload) reduce to < 0.2% of requests in 5m window within next deploy.
- No >100ms KV async-load observed in single-request queue (concurrency 1) in local smoke test after fix.

Notes-to-self:
- Keep this session short — wrap up by 1:00pm. Push a small metrics PR first so we get visibility before touching compaction.
- If time, draft the prewarm hook as a feature flag behind 'kv_preload_on_profile_change' and test with canary route.

Linkbacks:
- Jira ticket for visibility: RDM-2917 (linked above)
- Temp GH branch: ramon/kv-fast-prewarm (pushed, WIP)

End-of-lunch quick timeline:
- 12:10–12:30: repro, logs, hypothesis narrowing
- 12:30–12:55: two quick experiments (disable eviction, CPU pin), record metrics
- 12:55–13:00: write this note + open metric PR stub

Misc (random snippets):
- If we add a short-circuit for single-token sequences to skip compaction paths, ensure not to break multi-token pipelining when batching picks up.
- Consider adding lightweight priority queue for async-loads: small payloads first, compaction tasks low priority.

Next steps after lunch:
- Submit metrics PR and ping infra for a short canary with compaction off on a low-traffic pool.
- Draft the prewarm feature as a config flag and add unit test covering swap->prewarm flow.

-- Ramon
